Observations:  
- Channel 0 (agent) has large weights almost only in column 1, rows 1â8: e.g. (r2,c1)=7.10, (r1,c1)=6.48, (r6,c1)=4.98, (r7,c1)=5.22, (r8,c1)=4.68. This says the agent is a vertical object fixed on the left edge of the playable area, and the policy mainly needs to know its row.  
- Channel 1 (moving objects) has large weights across the playable area, with maxima like (r6,c3)=12.17, (r5,c2)=10.81, (r2,c2)=10.66, (r6,c2)=8.63. This suggests a ball or other moving object that travels around the grid.  
- Channel 2 (reward targets) has its strongest weights on the rightmost column, rows 1â8: e.g. (r6,c9)=0.97, (r2,c9)=0.85, (r4,c9)=0.82, (r5,c9)=0.82. This points to the right edge being the reward/goal side.  
- Channel 3 (obstacles) is high all around the outer ring, e.g. row 0 and row 9 are mostly 0.7â0.9, and column 0/9 are also high. This is just the wall border.  
- Channel 4 (previous frame) has strong weights across the playable area, e.g. (r8,c5)=13.82, (r1,c5)=10.59, (r7,c4)=9.35. This is used to infer motion/velocity from the previous position of the agent or moving object.  
- Output layer: biases are 0.931, 1.261, 1.065, 0.861, 0.855 for no-op/up/down/left/right. Up and down have the largest biases. Many W3 rows differentiate up vs down strongly, while left/right are often similar or weak. For example row 2 is `0.133 1.003 1.898 0.059 0.046`, favoring down; row 16 is `-0.056 1.178 1.165 -0.032 -0.068`, favoring up/down over left/right. This shows the policy cares mainly about vertical movement.

Reasoning:  
The agent being a vertical object fixed at column 1 rules out games where the player moves freely in 2D, such as Snake or a maze/collect game. It also rules out Breakout, where the paddle would be at the bottom and left/right actions would dominate. The strong moving-object channel across the whole playable area, the right-edge reward-target channel, and the up/down-focused action output all match Pong: the agent controls the left paddle, the ball moves around, and the right side is the goal/opponent side. The previous-frame channel is especially useful for estimating the ballâs trajectory.

Game: Pong.

Description: The agent controls the left paddle and moves it up/down to hit the ball; reward comes from getting the ball past the opponent/right side, while the opponent tries to return it.

Confidence: 95%
